summary: CoAct-1 delegates subtasks between a GUI operator and a programmer that executes Python or Bash. Its OSWorld evaluation studies a hybrid action space in which scripts handle suitable file and data operations while visual interaction handles other steps.

name: HarmonyGuard: Toward Safety and Utility in Web Agents via Adaptive Policy Enhancement and Dual-Objective Optimization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported policy-compliance and task-completion gains are from the paper’s benchmark evaluations.
summary: Introduces HarmonyGuard, a multi-agent framework that updates security policies and weighs safety against task completion for agents operating on the open web.

name: Uncertainty-Aware GUI Agent: Adaptive Perception through Component Recommendation and Human-in-the-Loop Refinement
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RecAgent narrows attention to recommended UI components and requests user feedback when task intent or decisions remain uncertain. It introduces ComplexAction to evaluate specified single-step GUI actions in difficult interface scenarios.

name: VeriWeb: Verifiable Long-Chain Web Benchmark for Agentic Information-Seeking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark focuses on web information seeking and synthesis.

name: Evolving in Tasks: Empowering the Multi-modality Large Language Model as the Computer Use Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Self-Evolution Agent combines automatic generation of verifiable computer-use trajectories with step-wise reinforcement learning for long-horizon training. It also describes a model-enhancement procedure that integrates grounding and planning capabilities without an additional training stage.

name: GuirlVG: Incentivize GUI Visual Grounding via Empirical Exploration on Reinforcement Learning
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot.
summary: Introduces GuirlVG, an empirical study of reinforcement fine-tuning for GUI visual grounding. It analyzes training components and adds an adaptive KL-based mechanism to limit reward over-optimization.

name: Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: D2Snap reduces serialized DOM observations while preserving actionable elements and features that distinguish their uses. The study compares reduced DOM inputs with screenshot-based observations for a web agent on tasks sampled from Online-Mind2Web.

name: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory

name: Flash-Searcher: Fast and Effective Web Agents via DAG-Based Parallel Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).

name: How To Train Your World Model: Fine-tuning vs RAG for LM-based World Modeling
notes: Adjacent cross-domain study with WebShop as its web evaluation. WebShop uses text-rendered search/product pages and an explicit valid-action menu. name: fastbrowse
notes: Python package fastbrowse 0.5.23 by Agent Labs (Python 3.13+), with a CLI, an MCP server (fastbrowse-mcp) and a JavaScript SDK. The browser layer speaks CDP through cdp-use; snapshot.js, ported from jev-ultrafast, indexes each frame's controls, viewport text and a freshness fingerprint, including open shadow roots. Per the design document, Jev chooses the operation and target among indexed controls (with relevance pruning on dense pages), an LLM proposes start addresses, plans checkable requirements, reads page text, writes non-secret field text and composes the answer, and code enforces freshness and hit-tests before input, no automatic retry of mutations, authorization for submit, pay, delete or send, secret redaction and budgets; a run counts as complete only when every requirement is evidenced. Browsers are Browser Use Cloud by default, local Chrome, or an existing CDP endpoint including Electron windows. Jev is reached through TypeSafe, OpenRouter or the Vercel AI Gateway. Benchmark comparisons in the README are the publisher's. Root LICENSE is MIT, with a NOTICE file.
summary: Browser agent in which TypeSafe's Jev picks each action from controls indexed on the page over CDP, an LLM plans and reads, and code gates inputs, secrets and irreversible steps; answers cite page quotes.

name: OpenJev
notes: Models and code for an open replacement of a hosted System One decision API. A Qwen3 or Qwen3.5 backbone without its vocabulary head scores each option with a pointer head, so one pass answers every question in a request; a local server exposes POST /v1/systemone. Browser steps arrive as page text, numbered elements and recent actions, and the model chooses an operation (click, type, DONE and others) and a target element. The repository holds the wev package (data conversion for Mind2Web, NNetNav and WebChain, training, calibration, export, serving), teacher-collection scripts, the OpenJev-Bench browser-lane client (2,346 frozen steps stored in the Hub dataset alanhuangya/OpenJev-Data), locked results and the paper source; the paper is a Zenodo deposit (doi 10.5281/zenodo.22941164) with no catalog record. The models also answer general decisions such as triage and routing. Results are publisher-reported, and live-website numbers use an LLM judge.

notes: Chrome Manifest V3 extension (manifest version 1.9.1) whose agent loop is built on the pi-agent-core and pi-ai packages. Its tools (src/agent/tools.ts) read a paginated inventory of interactive DOM controls including open shadow roots, inspect forms, click elements or screenshot-pixel coordinates (used for canvas editors such as Google Docs), type, scroll, switch and open tabs, upload files, post to social sites and send webmail; capture_tab_screenshot returns the visible-tab image to the model. notes: Python MCP server published by baryhuang and distributed as the Docker image buryhuang/mcp-remote-macos-use; the target Mac needs only Screen Sharing enabled, with host, username and password passed as environment variables. Its own RFB client (src/vnc_client.py) supports only Apple Authentication (protocol 30). server.py registers eight tools: remote_macos_get_screen (a PNG screenshot), send_keys, mouse_move, mouse_click, mouse_double_click, mouse_scroll, mouse_drag_n_drop and open_application; action handlers scale the client's coordinates to the remote screen size, and open_application types the app name into Spotlight (Command+Space, text, Return). An optional LiveKit handler adds WebRTC screen sharing when LiveKit variables are set. The server has no model of its own; the MCP client's model decides the actions. Root LICENSE is MIT (copyright peakmojo); the default branch was last committed on 30 April 2025.
summary: MCP server that lets an LLM client such as Claude Desktop control a remote Mac through its built-in Screen Sharing, returning screenshots and sending scaled mouse, keyboard, scroll and drag actions over VNC.

name: OpenBrowser
notes: Published on PyPI as openbrowser-ai. The CodeAgent (src/openbrowser/code_use/service.py) sends a compact serialized DOM state with element indices and, unless vision is turned off, a JPEG screenshot; the model replies with Python that the executor runs in a persistent namespace. The MCP server exposes a single execute_code tool over the same namespace, and a CLI daemon keeps a browser session alive between commands. The repository also holds a hosted-platform backend and frontend, and infra/training with SFT, online GRPO and diffusion-language-model RL code for FormFactory form filling; the README links the two related papers on ResearchGate. name: Browserable
notes: Inspected at commit a3af19a6 (27 August 2025). The README sets up a Docker Compose stack (UI server, tasks server, MongoDB, Redis and MinIO) in which the user supplies one LLM key (Gemini, OpenAI or Claude) and a Steel or Hyperbrowser key; tasks/services/browser.js also accepts Browserbase or the repository's own browser service, which launches Playwright Chromium. In tasks/agents/browserable.js the act-on-tab action calls simpleActionHelper, whose loop takes a plain page screenshot and the current chunk of DOM elements with XPaths, asks a planner for high-level steps (replanning after five steps), and asks a runner for a Playwright method, arguments and element number; the older DOM-only and vision act helpers are commented out at that call site. The repository also contains deep-research and generative agents. The README's 90.4% WebVoyager figure is publisher-reported. The README names Stagehand among the open-source projects it builds on. No code was run.

name: DomA
notes: The README presents DomA as a browser agent from Stay Browser, and the LICENSE notice names Dom Actions; the commercial store build adds video download, a userscript manager and ad blocking on top of this core. The service worker implements browser_* tools (tabs, navigation, page content, element lists, click, text click, type, select, scroll, script execution, clipboard). browser_screenshot tags up to 150 visible interactive elements with data-som-idx and composites numbers and borders onto a clean viewport capture, grouping the overflow into areas A1 to A5; clicks fall back to CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent through chrome.debugger. With the Jev switch on, a high-confidence Jev decision can execute a click or type without sending the image to the LLM. Models are user-supplied OpenAI-compatible endpoints. An MCP bridge (stdio server plus a local daemon on ports 3846/3847) and a CLI let Cursor, Claude or OpenClaw drive the extension.

name: Orca
notes: Published by echoVic as the npm package @blade-ai/orca and native binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows; it is primarily a coding agent that reads and edits code and runs commands with a DeepSeek API key. Computer use is one feature: on macOS 14 or later, in the main interactive TUI session, a `computer` tool backed by the bundled crates/orca-computer-use driver lists and launches apps, observes a window as an accessibility-element outline with ids plus an optional screenshot, and clicks, types, sends keys and scrolls on targets (protocol.rs, observation.rs). Per the computer-use docs, each app needs approval unless a rule or full-auto mode allows it, typing into secure password fields always asks separately, password managers and finance apps are blocked by default, Orca never operates its own host terminal, plan mode only lists and observes, and Esc stops the run. Browser tools used from the separate Pilion Browser come from that host. Root LICENSE is MIT; the latest GitHub release is v0.5.12.

name: FluidUse
notes: Published by FluidInference; the package targets macOS 14 or later. AccessibilityFormDriver snapshots the focused window of another running app through the macOS Accessibility API into form elements addressed by tokens, writes values through AXValue and presses buttons and checkboxes with AXPress; for Safari, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Firefox and similar browsers it sends real key events instead, because those apply AXValue writes to the focused field. WebFormDriver does the same for an embedded WKWebView through an injected script. FormSchema renders each field's context and a fixed option list (fill Label: value for each document entity, check, click, skip) for a model to score, and decodes the chosen option into an action. The README's form model is CUA-S1-FORMS, a 706K-parameter form specialist from Cua converted to Core ML; its manager (CuaS1FormsManager) comes from the FluidAudio package dependency. Most of the package consists of on-device Core ML runtimes for general typed-decision, classification, embedding and OCR models (laya, GLiNER 2.5, Kev, Clef, Intern-Decision, SigLIP2 and others) and demos such as Tetris and 2048 players; their scope lies outside GUI operation. Latency and accuracy figures in the README are publisher measurements. Root LICENSE is Apache-2.0; the latest release, v0.3.0, predates the inspected commit.

name: SMAN-Bench
notes: SMAN-Bench is the title of the ICLR 2026 edition of the Mobile-Bench-v2 paper; that edition's proceedings PDF gives this repository as its code and data location, and the README's dataset badge links the Hugging Face release xwk123/MobileBench-v2, which holds the task data. The repository itself has code only, no task files. AppAgent runners draw numbered boxes for clickable and scrollable elements, taken from each recorded page's XML, onto the screenshot; Mobile-Agent-v2 runners (memory unit on, reflection off by default) receive the centre coordinates of the same elements. Single-path and ambiguous runs step through the ground-truth page sequence whatever the agent chooses; multi-path runs move through the recorded page graph according to the agent's actions (default limit 20 rounds) and succeed on reaching the goal page. Ambiguous runs prompt with the task's vague instruction and per-step instructions, or with the complete instruction. eval.py has scorers for single-path, multi-path and noisy runs, printing task success rate, action accuracy and action-type accuracy; the noisy scorer checks the ground-truth click or swipe coordinates against the predicted element's bounds and typed text by character-level F1 above 0.5. Model endpoints are set in config/config.yaml. The README shows an MIT badge, but the tree at the reviewed commit has no LICENSE file. Not a fork, not archived; no release.
summary: Evaluation code for SMAN-Bench (Mobile-Bench-v2): AppAgent and Mobile-Agent-v2 runners replay recorded Android pages for single-path, multi-path, noisy and ambiguous tasks, scored by step and task success.

name: Shadow
notes: Requires Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or later and a source build (Swift 6, Rust, XcodeGen). GroundingOracle.swift resolves targets for the Mimicry replay system in four steps: exact accessibility-tree match, fuzzy accessibility match, a local ShowUI-2B model on MLX over a live screenshot, then a vision-model escalation. TrainingDataGenerator.swift turns recorded (screenshot, accessibility state, click) tuples into JSONL grounding examples, and LoRATrainer.swift fine-tunes ShowUI-2B on them through the mlx-vlm Python package once enough new tuples accumulate. The README describes the capture of fourteen signal types, on-device Qwen and Whisper models, a 26-tool agent runtime, and points to a separate computer-use engine from the same publisher for full computer use. Cloud model features are optional with the user's own API key.

notes: Kotlin app for Android 12 or later with an on-device ReAct loop, subagent delegation, todo and scratchpad tools, markdown memory files and per-app skills. Perception defaults to the accessibility tree; screenshot-only and hybrid modes are options (perception/PerceptionConfig.kt). Clicks try an accessibility ACTION_CLICK on the resolved node and fall back to a dispatched gesture tap (tool/action/ClickExecutor.kt, platform/NodeActionPerformer.kt, platform/AccessibilityGestureInjector.kt). Optional power tools use Shizuku for a background virtual display, Termux for a Linux shell, and Chrome DevTools Protocol scripting of Chrome. A bundled tier list blocks banking, payment, crypto-wallet, password-manager and authenticator packages (assets/security/app_tiers.json), and other apps need per-app approval. Models are reached through OpenAI-compatible endpoints or a ChatGPT/Codex sign-in. The eval/ harness drives AndroidWorld task setup and scoring and launches the app over ADB.

name: LongHorizonUI
notes: Code release of the ICLR 2026 paper "LongHorizonUI: A Unified Framework for Robust long-horizon Task Automation of GUI Agent" (the repository description says ICLR2026; the README cites it with anonymous authors and no link). Each screenshot passes through RapidOCR, the OmniParser v2 YOLO icon detector (downloaded from microsoft/OmniParser-v2.0 on first use) and template matching when an icon template directory is set; the merged elements are drawn as numbered boxes, and that annotated screenshot with a step prompt is what the Gemini, Azure OpenAI or OpenAI model receives. Actions are click, long press, swipe, drag, text input and key press. With the fallback cascade on (the default), an element-index target that fails is retried as a relative point inside the box and then as absolute coordinates with jitter; a progress monitor can roll back to the last committed snapshot, at most three times per task. The README documents only the offline mode, which replays a task's recorded screenshot sequence with either the task description or step-by-step instructions. run.py also has a live subcommand that lists USB-connected devices, but at the reviewed commit AndroidContext never opens a device connection (its context stays None), so device actions return without acting. The repository also has a Gradio app, agents that turn recorded taps and swipes into step descriptions, a scrcpy-based Android recording tool, step-level evaluation scripts and the project page source. The LongGUIBench dataset is not released (the README link is a placeholder), the requirements.txt the README installs from is not in the tree, and the README's Apache-2.0 badge and LICENSE link are not backed by a license file. Not a fork, not archived; no release.

name: Andee
notes: Kotlin Android app for Android 11 (API 30) or later, published by KUAFUAI, with a floating-ball persona, voice input and output, an encrypted on-device notebook and scheduled scenes. One AccessibilityService is the entry point. ScreenController.kt renders the pruned accessibility tree as an outline with one line per element, an element id, a clickable mark and a centre in 0-1000 relative coordinates; for apps that draw their own pixels the model gets a screenshot (accessibility takeScreenshot, or MediaProjection per ScreenCapture.kt) overlaid with an 8-column by 12-row labelled grid, taps by cell and which third of it, and can request a zoomed view with a red crosshair before committing. A per-location guard refuses a fourth tap within 120 px of the same spot inside five minutes. Text goes in through the accessibility input channel on Android 13 or later, with ADBKeyboard as the fallback. LocalBrain.kt runs a non-streaming tool-calling loop against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint for a configurable number of steps (1 to 200); the brain can instead run elsewhere and reach the device over a WebSocket hub. The README states that the dispatcher stops before a purchase's final confirmation, never enters payment passwords, and types vault passwords without returning them to the model. Optional extras include a robot dog driven through a USB OTG dongle. Root LICENSE is the Andee Open Source License: Apache-2.0 text with additional conditions (no white-labelling, no multi-tenant hosting, written authorisation to ship it inside another product); GitHub reports NOASSERTION. The README says ML Kit barcode and play-services stubs bundled with the app are not open source. Release v0.5.2 tags the inspected commit.

name: MemGUI-Bench
notes: Official benchmark code for the MemGUI-Bench paper (ACM MM 2026 per the README). The mg CLI pulls a prebuilt Docker runtime with the Android emulator and the MemGUI AVD snapshot, launches parallel backend containers on a Linux host with KVM, runs agents through MobileWorld's agent interface (src/mobile_world) and writes MobileWorld-format trajectories with screenshots. MemGUI-Eval (memgui_eval/) describes each step with a multimodal model and makes a final decision with a second model; the leaderboard uses Gemini 2.5 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Pro for these roles. Each task CSV row gives the app(s), difficulty, whether UI memory is required and golden steps; the default step budget is int(golden_steps * 2.5 + 1). The Hugging Face dataset lgy0404/MemGUI-Bench holds the same two task CSV files (byte-identical at revisions 217713e and 3fb01b6), so it is recorded as an alias.
summary: Memory-centric Android benchmark of 128 tasks across 26 apps, run in Dockerized emulators on a MobileWorld-style runtime and judged by MemGUI-Eval, an LLM evaluator reporting pass@k and memory metrics.

name: Odysseys
notes: Each task has a SHA-1 ID, a prompt, a starting URL, a difficulty level, a reference step count, numbered rubric items with requirement and verification text, and SimilarWeb category tags. The README runs tasks with the OSWorld runner (Chrome in an Ubuntu VM, 100-step budget) after converting them with convert_odysseys_to_osworld.py, whose OSWorld evaluator is a placeholder; scoring is done afterwards by run_full_trajectory_per_rubric.py, which asks an LLM judge (by default gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview, the model the README uses, or an OpenAI-compatible model) whether any step satisfies each rubric item. Reported metrics are the averaged rubric score, the perfect rate and trajectory efficiency. The README says the starting URL is always Google, but 70 of the 200 tasks in odysseys.json start at another site, and the converter opens each task's own URL. Tasks run on live websites, so results can drift. README results are paper figures.

name: Gelato
notes: There is no arXiv paper; the README's citation is a GitHub @misc entry. The README describes how Click-100k was filtered (OmniParser element checks, Qwen2.5-VL-7B difficulty and GTA1-7B-2507 alignment filters) and reports 63.88% on ScreenSpot-Pro, 69.15% on OS-World-G with refusal prompting, and 58.71 ± 0.66% automated OS-World success across three runs; none of these was reproduced. It also releases a UI-TARS-1.5-7B baseline trained with the same recipe as mlfoundations/Gelato-UI-TARS-1.5-7B, which has no model card. evaluation/os-world/gelato_agent.py is a modified GTA1.5 OSWorld agent: GPT-5 plans from screenshots and its tool calls become pyautogui commands, with click targets requested from a vLLM-served grounding model; it runs inside an OSWorld checkout. The repository has no license file.

name: Wanta
notes: Recorded as adjacent: Wanta is a general agent host whose local tools are files, shell, skills, knowledge and SaaS connectors (OpenConnector), and its only graphical executor is the integrated browser. The Electron main process owns a WebContentsView per task page, Playwright attaches through a custom CDP transport over webContents.debugger, and an authenticated loopback bridge serves seven OpenCode tools: browser_navigate, browser_read (title, URL, dialog state and a Playwright AI-mode ARIA snapshot with refs), browser_click and browser_type on refs or unique selectors, browser_scroll, browser_screenshot and browser_dialog. The user shares the page and completes logins and CAPTCHAs; in Default Access the agent is told to hand sensitive actions to the user, which the design document calls a behavioural policy rather than a system guarantee. External agents keep their own accounts; hosted models, connectors and team workspaces need an OOMOL account. Packages for macOS, Windows and Linux. Root LICENSE is Apache-2.0.

name: Bops
notes: Electron app (desktop/) that starts a local Next.js server (app/, lib/server/) on port 3210; version 0.0.28 in package.json, matching release tag v0.0.28 at 92ec73d, and the inspected commit 62c7f98 is later. Bots' tasks run on Orgo cloud computers launched from the bops-base template that orgo/bops-base.mjs builds from vm/ (Codex, the screen MCP and per-screen Chrome helpers). By default lib/server/computer-task.ts runs each thread on OpenAI's Responses API computer tool: Orgo's API returns a screenshot of the bot's screen, and every click, double-click, drag, scroll, typing or key press the model asks for is executed as xdotool commands through Orgo's bash endpoint, with the result screen sent back; the same loop offers a page_script tool that runs a short Playwright script on the screen's Chrome over CDP, a Linux shell, web search, a password vault and app, data and CRM tools. With BOPS_COMPUTER_TOOL=0 threads use OpenAI's Agents API with Codex and vm/screen_mcp.py, which exposes one screen's screenshot and input actions over MCP. Tasks on the user's own Mac run in a bot-owned Chrome; with Full access they also get a shell and the user's apps through Cua Driver behind vm/mac-ui-mcp.mjs, which hides sensitive apps, sends input only in the background and blocks quitting, copying and pasting (lib/server/local.ts). Per the README, reading runs at once while sending, creating and paying wait for the user's approval, and any screen can be watched live and taken over. Self-hosting requires an Orgo account and two OpenAI API keys, with Honcho, Composio, treg, AgentMail, AgentPhone and TypeSafe recommended or optional; signing in with Orgo instead routes provider calls through Orgo's hosted Bops Cloud (cloud/). Licensed FSL-1.1-ALv2 (fair source; competing products and hosted services are excluded, and each version becomes Apache-2.0 two years after release); components/message-ui/ is adapted from MIT-licensed code.

notes: Code for the OSReward paper; the trajectories themselves are released separately on Hugging Face as OS-Copilot/OSReward (the README reports 1,019 Full and 284 Hard trajectories with screenshots and human verdicts), alongside the gated OS-Shepherd-100K corpus and OS-Shepherd checkpoints. eval_pipeline/run_judge.py downloads the Full or Hard Parquet split (or reads local traces), sends a judge the full thought and action history and, by default, the last five screenshots with red markers at normalized action points, at temperature 0, through an OpenAI-compatible or native Anthropic API, and parses one 'Judge: SUCCESS' or 'Judge: FAIL' verdict per trajectory. It reports accuracy, balanced accuracy, SUCCESS and FAIL recall and coverage; missing, failed and unparseable outputs count as incorrect. Its subset option offers full, hard and custom, with no OSReward-Multi option, although the README roadmap lists Multi under the evaluation harness. trajectory_collection/ holds the collection pipelines: webtrail for live and self-hosted websites, a Windows Agent Arena based Windows 11 VM pipeline, an AndroidWorld based emulator pipeline, and an OSWorld based Ubuntu pipeline with a screenshot-only tool-call agent (the root README calls Ubuntu 'on the way' and the collection README calls it a placeholder, but its code is in the tree), plus export_judged_sft.py for judge-SFT bundles. benchmarking_analysis/ scores judges against the ground-truth labels of OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena, WebArena and AndroidWorld rollouts, with small samples under data/raw. The OS-Shepherd-100K construction pipeline and the OS-Shepherd training and inference code are listed as pending release. There is no root LICENSE; the bundled Windows and Android pipelines carry Microsoft's MIT and the Apache-2.0 license texts. Not a fork, not archived; no release.

name: Gemini Browser Agent
notes: The README calls the project a research experiment and scaffolding. websocket_agent.py is a local WebSocket server that calls gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025 through google-genai with the browser computer-use environment; widget/ is an unpacked Manifest V3 extension with a side panel where the user connects to the bridge and enters a goal. Each turn the extension captures the visible tab with chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab, the bridge converts the model's 0-1000 normalized coordinates to viewport pixels, and the extension carries out clicks, typing, key presses, hovering, scrolling and navigation by injecting functions (chrome.scripting.executeScript) that dispatch synthetic DOM events at document.elementFromPoint. Drag and drop is approximated with mousedown and mouseup events, unhandled model actions return an unimplemented warning, and the side panel sets a step limit (default 10). It needs a Gemini API key and acts in the user's own browser without a sandbox; the README points to the author's separate gemini-computer-use repository for sandboxed runs. The repository has no license file at the inspected commit.

name: AI Mime
notes: Requires macOS 13 or newer, Python 3.12 and Accessibility, Screen Recording and Input Monitoring permissions; Windows support remains pending. The recorder (pynput listeners and mss screenshots) writes a manifest of clicks, typing, hotkeys and scrolls with pre-action screenshots, plus optional extract and detail notes. Reflection turns the trace into a coordinate-free schema.json; an optimizer writes optimized_plan.json, preferring script steps, then browser_harness steps (Chrome CDP through a browser-harness git submodule), then ui_agent steps; a build agent packages a Claude Skill-compatible folder with run.sh, inputs and a fallback plan. The ui_agent drives the Mac in the foreground through cua-computer-server MCP tools, which AI Mime extends with combined screenshot-plus-accessibility-tree reads, and is told to target accessibility elements before screenshot coordinates. Agent runtimes are Anthropic (Claude Code) or OpenAI (Codex), selected during onboarding, with custom providers in user_config.yml. A prebuilt macOS DMG is linked from the README.

name: OpenComet
notes: The README presents it as a Smart India Hackathon entry for problem statement 26171, whose listed organisation is ISRO. The Manifest V3 extension (version 1.31.0 at review) is loaded unpacked in Chrome; the README says Firefox has been built from the same source since v1.17.0. src/content/dom-detector.js paints numbered boxes on interactive elements, and the service worker captures the tab through the Chrome debugger or captureVisibleTab, so screenshots carry those marks. In privacy mode, MediaPipe, YOLO, ViT, Tesseract OCR and regex/checksum PII detectors run in the browser, and src/lib/privacy-firewall.js blocks or blanks a frame when sanitizing fails. Actions use selectors, with debugger Input.dispatchMouseEvent clicks where needed, inside a tab-group sandbox with an approval mode. Models: on-device Gemma 4, cloud providers, or Ollama through the bundled server. OpenCometBench is the repository's own test suite; its PII precision/recall uses a synthetic corpus built from the detector's own rules, as the README states, leaving independence outside the measurement.

name: HarnessBench
notes: Sister project of ClawBench. The repository holds the harness-bench CLI (harness x model x task matrix expansion with credential gating, run, batch and a leaderboard renderer over ClawBench result summaries), six harness adapters (openclaw, hermes, claw-code, browser-use, stagehand, coze-studio), each a Dockerfile, setup script and run script built on the clawbench-base image, and a one-task smoke fixture. The tasks, the five-layer recording and the judge belong to ClawBench; this repository holds the harness, whose run and batch commands call clawbench.run_case and require clawbench-eval 0.2.0 or later. At the inspected commit the README's fixtures/lite.txt 20-task subset is absent from the tree, the browser-use run script calls a run-browser-use.py that neither the tree nor its Dockerfile supplies, and the leaderboard and demo videos are placeholders. stagehand and coze-studio need BrowserBase or Coze credentials.

name: jev-use
notes: The Swift app (built as Desktop Voice.app; macOS 14.2+ and Xcode) reads the front window's Accessibility tree, skipping secure text fields, and sends the command, app and window names, numbered targets and recent actions to TypeSafe's hosted systemone endpoint with model jev-latest; no screenshots are sent (Sources/JevDesktop/Desktop.swift, Sources/JevCore/Decision.swift). Actions use Accessibility presses and value setting plus CGEvent mouse, key and scroll events. An optional OpenRouter key enables a planner model (default inception/mercury-2.5) that splits a spoken command into steps; Jev still chooses each on-screen target (Sources/JevCore/Planner.swift). Input is Apple Speech hold-to-talk, hands-free mode, an optional "Hey Jev" wake phrase, or typed commands. The README says low-confidence and destructive picks stop and ask. Jev is a hosted model.

name: Xiryn
notes: Next.js app run locally (version 0.4.1 in package.json; tag v0.4.1 points at b8016b5, and the inspected commit 489e9c4 is later). Each agent's workstation is a Docker container built from workstation/: Debian (trixie-slim) with Xvfb, xfwm4 and a panel, Chromium, x11vnc and noVNC, xdotool and scrot, a persistent home volume, and an inactivity watchdog. lib/agent/tools.ts defines the tool belt for the Vercel AI SDK streamText loop: shell and fs_* through docker exec; screen_capture and screen_share (scrot JPEG through xiryn-shot); pointer_click, pointer_move, pointer_drag, pointer_scroll, key_type and key_press (xdotool in lib/workstation.ts), each returning a fresh screenshot; request_takeover; vault_list, vault_fill, request_payment_approval and request_secret; memory_write and memory_forget; web_search and web_fetch through Firecrawl; and delegate for squads. Observation is plain screenshots of a 1280x800 display with pixel coordinates; there is no accessibility tree or element annotation. Before each step the runtime keeps only the two most recent screenshots in full (docs/architecture.md). The vault fills saved logins and cards into fields without the model seeing them, and cards only after the owner approves the payment. The user can watch and take over the desktop, and the agent hands over at logins, payments, one-time codes or CAPTCHAs, with a Telegram notice when paired. Models come from the owner's keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The README's comparison with hosted agents is the author's own. Root LICENSE is MIT.

name: System1-Agents
notes: Adjacent because browser and desktop control are two of several shipped domains; the package (s1a) is equally aimed at games, ALFWorld, ticket routing and an injection-guard rail. On a decision turn the System 1 model answers typed choice questions while a chat model keeps planning, typed values and the final answer. The browser front runs a stock openJiuwen browser subagent (pinned ThinkFlowLab fork of agent-core) over @playwright/mcp; its in-page probe numbers the visible controls of the top document's light DOM, and the decision model chooses an element plus an operation head (CLICK, TYPE_TEXT, PRESS_ENTER, SELECT, scrolling). OmniJev instead receives a page screenshot. The desktop agent drives a Windows or macOS app window through the external Cua Driver over MCP, clicking accessibility elements bound to a window snapshot. Decision models are reached through TypeSafe, OpenRouter or served endpoints; Cua-S1 Nano runs in process from a pinned trycua/cua subdirectory. Speed and cost tables in the README are the publisher's single-episode comparisons. The browser files carry Huawei copyright notices with ThinkFlowLab modifications under Apache-2.0.

notes: Coding is the primary purpose: the README frames release v0.0.1 (Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or later, locally signed and not notarized) around a describe, investigate, edit, review and verify loop, and calls browser and desktop automation experimental. server.mjs runs an eido-browser MCP server with browser_* tools. name: Roubao
notes: Kotlin Android app (minimum SDK 26) published by Turbo1123. Shizuku gives it ADB-level shell access without root, which DeviceController.kt uses for screencap, input tap/swipe/text and am start; the agent's floating overlay is hidden while each plain screenshot is taken. In the default mode MobileAgent.kt runs Manager (plan), Executor (one of click, double_tap, long_press, type, swipe, system_button, open_app, wait, take_over or answer, with pixel coordinates), ActionReflector (compares the before and after screenshots) and an optional Notetaker over an OpenAI-compatible VLM API, for at most 25 steps by default; the README calls this layer a Kotlin port of Mobile-Agent-v3. Two other modes call GUI-Owl through Alibaba Cloud DashScope's GUI agent endpoint (default model pre-gui_owl_7b), which returns actions directly, or an OpenAI-compatible MAI-UI server (default localhost:8000, MAI-UI-2B) with MAI-UI's prompt format and up to three history screenshots. A Skills layer (app/src/main/assets/skills.json) can instead hand a request to another app through a deep link, and Tools cover app search, deep links, clipboard, shell and HTTP. When screencap is blocked on a secure screen the agent asks the user before continuing; the Manager prompt stops the run when a screen actively asks for payment confirmation, a password or biometric verification, and the Executor can hand logins and captchas to the user (take_over) or ask for confirmation of payment actions. The README says a 2.0 version based on AccessibilityService is developed on a separate branch; this record describes main. Root LICENSE is MIT; latest release V1.4.2.

name: Browser Agent (uiuing)
notes: Chrome Manifest V3 extension by uiuing, first released as v0.0.1 (Chrome zip in GitHub releases). The model acts on pages only through the page_act tool, which hands a goal to an engine that builds a semantic snapshot of DOM nodes with roles, accessible names, values, occlusion, open shadow roots and same-origin iframes (packages/extension/src/engine/page/perception.ts), resolves targets by fingerprint against a fresh snapshot and fires click, input, change and key events in the page (engine/page/execute.ts). The page_screenshot tool shows a capture to the user; its description limits the model to other page information rather than the pixels (tools/page.ts). A chrome.debugger channel is used for file uploads and falls back to DOM synthesis. Tools carry read, act or dangerous risk tiers with site allow/block lists and confirmation; verified runs can be saved as skills and replayed over batch rows. Model ports cover OpenAI-compatible, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic APIs. The docs/benchmark.md comparison is publisher-run on the project's own fixtures against its own replica of a viewport-only baseline.

name: Webagent (webagent.cloud)
notes: Open-source code of the webagent.cloud hosted service, published by webagent-cloud. A FastAPI server (server.py, webagent/api.py) with a bundled React UI accepts a prompt and runs it with the engine set by ENGINE_PROVIDER: Browser Use by default, or Notte, whose agent is fixed to gemini-2.5-flash with at most 30 steps. The browser comes from BROWSER_PROVIDER: a local Playwright Chromium over CDP, Browserbase or Steel; at the reviewed commit the Steel provider's create_session takes a context argument that the caller omits. Models are reached through Browser Use's chat clients for OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, Google and Groq; other provider values fall back to the OpenAI client. After a run, workflow_builder_service.py asks an LLM to extract parameters from the prompt and template the recorded actions with their element XPaths; workflow_replay_service.py replays those steps with Playwright (navigation, search, XPath clicks and typing, scrolling, key presses, uploads, dropdowns) without a model and, when an action fails, hands that step to the AI engine for up to three attempts. Tasks, runs and results are kept in a local SQLite database; results can be text or JSON validated against a supplied JSON Schema, and a webhook can be called on completion. The README's n8n, Zapier and Make integrations and Stagehand engine are not in the tree. Root LICENSE is MIT.
summary: Self-hostable browser-agent server that runs Browser Use or Notte agents, turns a run's recorded actions into a parameterized workflow, and replays it with Playwright, falling back to the agent when a step fails.

Although the README describes the full stack, the tree has no Python source: there is no backend/main.py, the server notes refer to main.py and pyxcursor.py files that are absent, and backend/agents is a git submodule pointing to xlang-ai/computer-agent-arena-hub, which the GitHub API did not return at review (404). The CSV has 2,010 verified two-agent sessions started between 2025-02-13 and 2025-05-15 (1,070 Windows, 940 Ubuntu; 653 distinct user IDs) with user-written task instructions, each agent's model and method, per-step feedback and the battle result (751 and 644 wins for the first and second agent, 615 ties). Agents in it are Claude 3.5 and 3.7 Sonnet computer use, OpenAI computer-use-preview, UI-TARS-1.5, a Qwen2.5-VL-72B agent, and GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, o3, o4-mini and Gemini models through a base agent. The frontend evaluation form asks for each agent's correctness (correct, partially correct, wrong) and a pairwise preference (A better, tie, B better, tie with both bad). The README shows an MIT badge and links a LICENSE file, but the tree has no root license file; its only license texts are those of the bundled noVNC viewer. Not a fork, not archived; no release.

name: dassi
notes: Omnify Labs of San Francisco builds dassi. The documentation says the agent identifies elements by role, text and position, can run JavaScript in the page, uses screenshots to verify its work and to handle coordinate-based interfaces, and asks the user to approve a plan before visiting new domains or acting on sensitive pages; passwords, payment details and CAPTCHA solving are outside its stated actions. The homepage describes teaching a job once, scheduled runs in the user's open browser, an editable memory of corrections and per-site JavaScript helpers the agent writes for itself, while the documentation's limitations page still says it does not run tasks in the background or on a schedule. name: WebOlympus: An Open Platform for Web Agents on Live Websites
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the ACL Anthology landing page and proceedings PDF. The platform observes HTML and screenshots and grounds actions through textual choices, set-of-mark overlays or pixel coordinates. On 50 Mind2Web tasks run on live websites, the paper reports SeeAct success of 48% with textual choices and 56% with set-of-mark grounding. The paper says code will be released for research under an OPEN-RAIL license; no release was checked in this review.

name: Accio Work
notes: Recorded as adjacent: the publisher presents Accio Work, powered by Alibaba, as an agent team for small and medium businesses covering market research, sourcing, storefront operation and marketing, and browser control is one of its tool sets. The Agent Tools Guide lists browser operations (clicks, navigation, screenshots and scripts) in the Full capability preset used by the Coder and Shopify Dropshipper templates, marked as requiring authorization; browser operations need user approval by default. The Browser Use Guide connects agents to the user's own logged-in browser either through the Accio Browser Relay extension, loaded unpacked from the Accio Work installation into any Chromium browser, or through Direct CDP (beta) on Chrome, over a local 127.0.0.1 connection with token authentication. Other tools cover files, terminal commands, web search and fetch, image generation and analysis, scheduled tasks and multi-agent group chats. The /work landing page is a client-rendered app whose HTML changes on every request, so the receipts are the publisher's static help documents.
summary: Agent workspace powered by Alibaba for small-business sourcing, store operations and marketing, whose agents can operate the user's own Chromium browser to navigate, click, type, take screenshots and extract data.

dataset_profile.notes: Project-page scope: screenshots paired with augmented view hierarchies, gesture coordinates, layout vectors and metadata. These observations describe screens paired with metadata; action and task totals use different units. The later semantic-annotation download augments the same screen corpus. The retained original paper reports more than 72k screens from more than 9.7k apps while this project page says more than 66k screens and more than 9.3k apps; the difference is unresolved. name: Rico
notes: The official project page cites the 2017 Rico paper. The project page reports more than 66,000 screens, while the original publication reports more than 72,000. The retained paper and project page report separate screen and app counts; the reason for their difference remains unresolved. App counts also differ: the official project page reports more than 9.3k Android apps and the retained published abstract more than 9.7k. Profile counts use the project-page scope; no reconciliation is inferred.
summary: Mobile app screenshots, view hierarchies, and interaction traces for UI research.

name: CLM-v0.1-8B
notes: The repository holds the CLM_v0.1-8B.pt head checkpoint and config; it needs Qwen3-8B embeddings served separately and the contrastive-lm package. License Apache 2.0.
summary: Weights for CLM-8B, a contrastive model with state and action heads on a frozen Qwen3-8B encoder that ranks candidate actions; the authors report computer-use, gaming and tool-calling results.

name: Fintor/Fintor-GUI-S2
notes: The card says training used SFT and LoRA and declares an Apache 2.0 license. The repository file list contains Safetensors weight shards and processor files.

name: GUI-360
summary: Desktop GUI trajectory data supporting multiple interface understanding tasks.

name: GUI-Owl 1.5 2B Instruct
notes: Hub API at revision 528ceaec lists one BF16 safetensors file (about 2.13B parameters) in the Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration architecture; access is open. The card is written for the whole GUI-Owl 1.5 family (instruct and thinking variants from 2B to 32B) and links the X-PLUG/MobileAgent repository; its tool/MCP, memory and multi-agent claims are family-level. For this checkpoint the card reports 43.5 on OSWorld-Verified, 67.9 on AndroidWorld, 33.0 on OSWorld-MCP, 31.3 on Mobile-World and 25.8 on WindowsAA; these are publisher measurements. The card declares MIT for the checkpoint; it gives no Hub base_model metadata.
summary: Smallest instruct checkpoint of GUI-Owl 1.5, a Qwen3-VL-based native GUI agent family from Mobile-Agent-v3.5 for desktop, mobile and browser tasks, usable alone or as a role in that framework.

name: Simular
summary: Computer-use products and research from Simular.

name: GUI-Actor 3B Qwen2.5-VL
notes: The card's heading says GUI-Actor-7B with a Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, but its metadata, text and usage code name Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct and this repository; the API reports 3,787,653,120 BF16 parameters and the Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGenerationWithPointer class, which loads through the gui_actor package. The Hub manifest lists two Safetensors shards, an index and trainer_state.json. ScreenSpot results in the card are publisher-reported. MIT is the card's weight declaration; Qwen2.5-VL and training-data terms are separate.

name: GUI-Lasagne L1
notes: Public archive shards are present. The dataset card declares Apache-2.0; it does not resolve rights in third-party interface content. The short card supplies no reliable sample count or explicit train/test partition, so these remain unspecified. An associated SpiritSight model card still describes dataset release as forthcoming; the independent dataset card and public archive manifest establish this release's availability.
summary: The published GUI-Lasagne training-data collection used for SpiritSight, distributed as dated archive shards for visual interface learning.

name: FluidGPT
notes: The page offers recordings for nine selected tasks and links to a full verification report. The completion figures are Fluiz's reported results.
summary: Android agent product presented through recorded AndroidWorld runs. Fluiz reports completion of 116 tasks across 20 apps through screen interaction.

name: Rico Dataset
notes: The site describes a platform for collecting, managing, and sharing mobile interaction datasets and invites contributions or self-hosting. It also states that 10k pieces of private user data are protected.
summary: Rico Dataset is a collection of mobile app interaction and design data presented through Interaction Mining, with 70k screens and 10k user flows across 5k apps.

name: Holo3.1 35B-A3B
notes: Hub API at revision 2bdb9285 lists 26 BF16 safetensors shards (about 35.1B parameters) in the Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration architecture; access is open. The card is written for the whole Holo3.1 family (0.8B, 4B, 9B and 35B-A3B) and names web, desktop and mobile without a mobile operating system. Its YAML base_model lists Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and three Qwen3.5 sizes while its prose says the Qwen 3.5 family, so base_model is unset. FP8, NVFP4 and GGUF quantizations are separate Hub repositories outside this record. Benchmark results appear only as images and are not recorded. The card declares Apache-2.0 for the weights.
summary: 35B-A3B checkpoint of H Company's Holo3.1 family, a sparse mixture-of-experts vision-language model for web, desktop and mobile computer use with native function calling.

notes: Hub revision 0bf2eb71 lists the card and 75 train Parquet shards; access is open. The card names desktop, web, mobile and operating-system interfaces without naming a mobile OS. Each row keeps a source-dataset tag and the original caption; the card does not describe how the description, function and combined instruction fields were produced, and no rows were downloaded. The card asks users to cite GTA1 and the five source datasets but does not say which GTA1 checkpoint was trained on this release. No license is declared for the compilation itself.

name: Cekura
notes: Customers send their documentation as it is together with an account for the product, and the agent checks the materials against the live product. The page's FAQ, rendered from its script bundle, calls Cekura an AI web agent that keeps SaaS product documentation up to date for knowledge and customer success teams, says the team sets up the service personally, and says model providers retain no data. The page publishes no self-serve signup, pricing or technical documentation; contact is by email or a booked call. A separate site, cekura.ai, presents a Cekura product for testing voice and chat AI agents; the relationship to cekura.io remains unspecified. Nothing was run.
summary: Service whose browser agent navigates a customer's SaaS product to check whether its documentation is still accurate, then reports what to fix with summaries, session replays and LLM and browser action traces.

name: PSAI computer-use dataset
notes: Released by Paradigm Shift AI. The card's apache-2.0 declaration covers this release and does not settle rights to the app screenshots.

Demonstrations come from splits.json, whose seven splits are disjoint; its iid_all list is the union of valid and test_iid and overlaps those splits. Turn records are rows of the chat configuration, one per evaluated navigator turn, a different unit from demonstrations; the train file exceeds the catalog's 10 MB evidence budget, leaving its turn-record count unrecorded. The card's extra test split duplicates test_iid. The counts cover demonstrations and chat turn records; reranking files and CSVs fall outside those counts. Screenshots are not in this repository.

name: WebLINX dataset
notes: The WebLINX repository README calls this the official dataset page and its library loads the data. The main revision a30ff2cb holds the preprocessed chat and reranking configurations, per-split CSV files, splits.json and prompt templates; the card points to a separate McGill-NLP/WebLINX-full repository for the complete raw demonstrations outside this record. The card describes WebLINX 1.1, a reprocessed BrowserGym release in another Hub repository, and links this original release as the v1.0 tag. CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 with added terms of use is the card's data declaration; the code repository's Apache-2.0 license is separate.

name: InternVL3_5-8B-HF

summary: InternVL3.5-8B multimodal model in Hugging Face Transformers format; its report evaluates the family on GUI grounding and on online agent tasks in OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena and WebArena-Lite-v2.

name: Skyvern Cloud
summary: Hosted Skyvern service for AI browser workflows such as invoice downloads and form filling, with built-in CAPTCHA and 2FA handling, proxy geotargeting, run explanations and JSON or CSV output.

notes: The public manifest contains 26 safetensors shards for the BF16 checkpoint and the card declares Apache-2.0. Quantized FP8/NVFP4/GGUF variants belong to the same model release. The card also contains demos and scores for Holo4-27B. No training corpus or runtime was downloaded.
summary: A Qwen3.6-based computer-use checkpoint designed to request GUI actions, code execution and tool calls through an external agent harness.

summary: Mobile-agent checkpoint based on Qwen3.6-27B for GUI and app-native tool interaction.

name: Do GUI Grounders Truly Understand UI Elements?
notes: The benchmark uses an automatic pipeline to generate and validate multiple instructions per UI element. Evaluation covers 12 models; the authors report up to 84% success in generating instructions that defeat grounding models.
summary: A desktop GUI grounding benchmark tests whether models identify the same element across varied descriptions; a diagnosis agent generates difficult instructions using model feedback.

details.training_data_note: The card states supervised fine-tuning on 700K human-annotated desktop examples from the GroundCUA dataset, followed by RLOO reinforcement learning with GUI-grounding rewards.

name: GroundNext-7B-V0
notes: The card's model is trained on desktop data only and reports publisher-run results on desktop grounding benchmarks and on mobile and web benchmarks (MMBench-GUI, ScreenSpot-v2). Its limitations say the model currently supports mouse clicks only, while the repository's groundcua.py system prompt declares a full computer_use tool schema with keyboard, scroll and drag actions. A 3B GroundNext model appears in the card's OSWorld table, but ServiceNow has not published a 3B checkpoint on the Hub. The Hub manifest lists four Safetensors shards and an index, and the API reports a Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration config with 8,292,166,656 BF16 parameters (the card states 7.0B). Apache-2.0 is the card's weight declaration and is not extended to the base model or training data.
summary: GroundNext GUI-grounding checkpoint fine-tuned from Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with SFT then RLOO on GroundCUA desktop data; it maps a screenshot and instruction to a computer_use click call.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Publisher supplies original, action, description and negative instruction types; no common end-to-end success metric is asserted.
benchmark_protocol.notes: Reuses ScreenSpot-v2 imagery. Image-file counts, independent screenshots and tasks are different units.

name: ScreenSpot-v2 instruction variants
notes: Public image files and desktop/mobile/web annotation JSON files are listed. This is a changed instruction set over an existing screenshot collection. No data license or precise example count is declared in the card; no paper relationship is inferred from its generic project/PDF links.

name: GUI-Owl 1.5 4B Instruct
notes: Hub API at revision 3f061c2c lists two BF16 safetensors shards plus an index (about 4.44B parameters) in the Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration architecture; access is open. The card is written for the whole GUI-Owl 1.5 family (instruct and thinking variants from 2B to 32B) and links the X-PLUG/MobileAgent repository; its tool/MCP, memory and multi-agent claims are family-level. For this checkpoint the card reports 48.2 on OSWorld-Verified, 69.8 on AndroidWorld, 31.7 on OSWorld-MCP, 32.3 on Mobile-World and 29.4 on WindowsAA; these are publisher measurements. The card declares MIT for the checkpoint; it gives no Hub base_model metadata.
summary: 4B instruct checkpoint of GUI-Owl 1.5, a Qwen3-VL-based native GUI agent family from Mobile-Agent-v3.5 for desktop, mobile and browser tasks, usable alone or as a role in that framework.

name: GLM-4.6V
notes: The Hugging Face repository hosts model weights and gives Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang usage instructions. The card declares an MIT license.
summary: GLM-4.6V is a vision-language model whose release describes screenshot-based tool use and reconstruction and editing of web interfaces from UI images.

name: ScaleCUA (THUDM) Qwen3-VL-8B OSWorld
notes: Hub API at revision d27cdab2 lists four BF16 safetensors shards (about 8.77B parameters) in the Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration architecture; access is open. The card calls this the online-RL (RLVR) checkpoint and names extreme1228/ScaleCUA-qwen3-vl-osworld-sft as its start point, which is also its Hub base_model. The card and the THUDM/SCALE-CUA README report 67.7% on OSWorld; this is a publisher figure. The card YAML declares license 'other' and its prose says the weights are released for research and inherit the license of Qwen3-VL-8B; that license is not resolved here. This project is distinct from OpenGVLab/ScaleCUA.
summary: Qwen3-VL-8B computer-use agent checkpoint from THUDM's ScaleCUA, trained with online RL for OSWorld desktop tasks after a released SFT start point.

name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
notes: The page says developers can access the model as claude-sonnet-4-5 through the Claude API. Its computer-use result and browser demonstration are publisher reports.
summary: Claude Sonnet 4.5 is a general model available through an API. Anthropic reports its computer-use performance on OSWorld and demonstrates browser tasks.

name: Adept Fuyu-Heavy
notes: Announced on January 24, 2024 as the model for Adept's enterprise product. The post includes text, chat and multimodal benchmark tables and a UI-understanding demo video.
summary: Adept multimodal model that scales up the Fuyu architecture for digital agents, aimed mainly at UI understanding; Adept reports MMMU, VQAv2, AI2D and ChartQA scores against Gemini models.

name: GUI-SD-data
notes: The repository holds an images/ folder of PNG screenshots and anno.jsonl in a single train split, with no dataset card or license. The GUI-SD repository's ms-swift training script loads the data through its --dataset argument.
summary: Training data for GUI-SD, an on-policy self-distillation method for GUI grounding, with about 6.99k screenshots and a JSONL annotation file read by the GUI-SD training scripts.

name: ClawGUI-2B
notes: A single model.safetensors file with tokenizer, processor and chat-template configs; the card declares Apache-2.0. The ClawGUI README also links a ModelScope copy, and the ClawGUI repository holds the RL training, evaluation and deployment code.
summary: ClawGUI-2B, a 2B mobile GUI agent model trained end to end with the ClawGUI-RL pipeline and GiGPO; the authors report a 17.1 MobileWorld success rate against an 11.1 baseline.

name: GT-r1
notes: Four safetensors shards plus a data&evaluate folder with data_train.json (1,593 items), data_test.json (177 items), a Defective_Open_Source archive and model_evaluate.py; the card declares Apache-2.0.
summary: A GUI defect detection model trained with VLM-R1 reinforcement learning that inspects an app screenshot and labels it as a content display error, UI layout issue, missing UI element or no defect.

name: Strawberry
notes: Strawberry Browser Inc., a Stockholm-based team, publishes Strawberry. On the browser-agent page a companion plans the work, opens the sites, moves between tabs, clicks through flows and uses an app integration when that is faster than browsing. Regular browsing is free, while companion work draws on monthly credits, with a free plan of 500 credits and paid tiers.
summary: Agentic desktop browser for macOS and Windows whose AI companions open sites, click through flows and work inside the user's signed-in accounts, asking for approval before sending, paying or deleting.

name: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking
notes: The release provides model weights and a Transformers inference example. The card declares an Apache 2.0 license.
summary: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking is a vision-language checkpoint whose card describes recognizing interface elements and using tools to operate PC and mobile GUIs.

name: Mano-CUA-2.0-4B
notes: The card identifies this as the full-precision checkpoint based on Qwen3-VL-4B and provides a Transformers inference example. It declares an Apache 2.0 license.
summary: A released GUI action model that takes a desktop screenshot and task context to produce structured actions, including clicks, typing, scrolling and app launches.

name: Webfuse
notes: Webfuse serves an existing website through a configurable proxy session and injects Extensions on the client side without changes to the site's code. Its Automation API, callable from an Extension, provides perception (DOM snapshot, Base64 screenshot of the page, accessibility tree, text selection) and actuation (click, type, scroll, select, key press, mouse move, text selection), targeting an element, CSS selector, point coordinate or Webfuse element ID across shadow DOM and iframes; the screenshot method is documented for Chromium-based browsers only. The Session MCP Server exposes the same tools, plus navigate and page info, to MCP clients authenticated with a Space automation key. tool.applyD2Snap() applies the DOM downsampling method of arXiv 2508.04412, whose second author, Nicholas Piël, is named on the about page as Webfuse's CEO and founder; the about page also says Webfuse grew out of the team's Surfly session technology. The pricing page lists Spark and Forge monthly plans metered in virtual minutes, a custom Foundry tier and a 14-day free trial.
summary: Web augmentation proxy that serves a site inside the user's browser and lets AI agents read DOM, screenshot or accessibility-tree snapshots and click, type or scroll through an automation API and a session MCP server.

name: Holo3.1 9B
notes: Hub API at revision bcd6a36a lists four BF16 safetensors shards (about 9.41B parameters) in the Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration architecture; the repository is publicly accessible. The card is shared by the whole Holo3.1 family (0.8B, 4B, 9B and 35B-A3B) and names web, desktop and mobile without a mobile operating system. Its YAML base_model lists Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and three Qwen3.5 sizes while its prose says the Qwen 3.5 family, so base_model is unset. name: Predicate Systems (formerly SentienceAPI)
notes: Predicate Systems Inc. was formerly SentienceAPI; www.sentienceapi.com redirects to this site. It has three parts. Predicate Authority is a Rust sidecar that evaluates local YAML policies and issues signed mandates before an action executes. Predicate Runtime, with Python and TypeScript SDKs, collects element geometry through a browser extension, gives the model a structured snapshot of element IDs, roles, text, importance scores and boxes (about 0.6-1.2k tokens per step by the publisher's estimate), executes the chosen action and runs assertions such as url_contains or exists; it runs standalone with Playwright or under browser-use, and an optional Gateway reranks elements with ONNX models. predicate-secure wraps frameworks such as browser-use, Playwright and LangChain with both checks. The documentation also covers Predicate Studio traces and Predicate Vault. New accounts start with 100 free credits.
summary: Runtime trust layer for browser agents: a sidecar checks each action against local policy before it runs, and SDKs turn pages into compact ranked element snapshots and verify outcomes with DOM assertions.

name: Retriever AI (rtrvr.ai)
notes: Retriever AI describes its engine as DOM-native: a planner directs sub-agents for clicks, typing and navigation, DOM extraction, pagination and files, and the same agent runs in the Chrome extension, in Cloud headless browsers (logins carried over by Cookie Sync) and through the API. Free Mode includes supported models and cloud browser time with sponsored cards and a daily allowance; users can bring their own model keys, and schedules, triggers, Cookie Sync and API or MCP control of the user's own Chrome require a paid plan. Recordings capture DOM interactions and the page's own network calls in place of screen recordings, and can be turned into replays or into subroutines that call a site's endpoints directly. An experimental Jev option lets a separate model choose browser actions while the selected model plans. The company also offers Rover, an agent that site owners embed for their visitors, and sells browser-agent trajectories and replica business apps for evaluation. The homepage's Web Bench ranking is a publisher claim.
summary: Browser agent from Retriever AI that runs in a Chrome extension on the user's signed-in sessions or in cloud browsers, reading page structure to click, type and fill forms; also callable through an API and MCP.

name: NNetNav Live data
notes: The Hub card supplies a license but no detailed schema. Dataset purpose is supported by the project's README; exact sample counts and annotation quality remain unverified.
summary: Browser-interaction data released with NNetNav for its live-website setting, with separate training and test files.

name: Mind2Web 2 task data and judge scripts
notes: The Hub API at revision 54f5b254 reports gated 'auto' (access is approved automatically after a logged-in request) and lists dev_set.csv and test_set.csv as the dev_set and test_set splits, a changelog, and 130 Python files under evaluation_scripts/2025_10_23. The description comes from the project README, which links this dataset as its tasks and judge-agent evaluation scripts and says the scripts for both the public dev set and the test set were released on 2025-10-23. The Hub card metadata declares CC BY 4.0; the repository code is MIT and is not applied to the data. Per the README, scoring with the scripts needs model API keys, and precaching the cited webpages is optional but recommended.
summary: Auto-gated Hub release of Mind2Web 2: dev and test task CSVs for long-horizon agentic web search, plus 130 per-task Python evaluation scripts that act as its judge agents.

name: Kura
notes: The homepage says Kura is backed by Y Combinator and lists client-side encryption, stealth browsers, proxy management, credential handling and audit trails. The documentation says the Recursion agent executes each plain-language instruction on the web page in real time and adds the matching blocks to a workflow; Action blocks click, type, press keys and refresh, go back or open, close and switch tabs, alongside navigation, extraction, checkpoint (natural-language assertion), for-loop and conditional blocks. Action and navigation blocks cache the elements or URLs they used and fall back to full reasoning when a cached step fails. A deployed agent gets synchronous and asynchronous API endpoints. The benchmarks page reports 87.0% on 602 of WebVoyager's 643 tasks (41 removed as impossible, booking, login or print tasks) and 90% against 56% for Anthropic's computer-use demo on 50 sampled tasks, for a hierarchical agent of planners, an executor and critics that runs mainly on GPT-4o; these figures are publisher-reported.
summary: Enterprise browser-agent builder whose Recursion agent runs plain-language steps on the live page and saves them as workflow blocks (actions, navigation, extraction, checks) with cached selectors, deployable as APIs.

name: Captioner
notes: The repository file list includes a PyTorch model file. The card provides no architecture or evaluation details.

name: Beam
notes: The homepage presents Beam as compute for agents: persistent, forkable microVMs that pause and resume, alongside GPU inference endpoints, task queues and sandboxes, and an MCP server whose tools create VMs, run commands and take screenshots, click and type on the desktop. The VM documentation says the default VM runs Ubuntu 24.04 with 4 CPUs and 8 GiB RAM, that `beam vm new` adds a desktop to fresh images, and that VMs are CPU-only. The desktop documentation covers screenshots, display resizing, mouse moves, clicks, X11 key presses, pasted text, scrolling, dragging, launching GUI programs and recording the guest screen from Python, JavaScript and the CLI; the desktop browser is Chrome on x86-64 and Firefox on ARM64. The homepage footer links the beam-cloud/beta9 repository (serverless GPU inference, sandboxes and background jobs, AGPL-3.0 per the GitHub API); whether it contains the VM desktop was not checked.
summary: Serverless cloud for AI workloads whose persistent microVMs for agents can include a Linux desktop with a browser that the SDKs, CLI and an MCP server operate through screenshots, clicks, key presses and typing.

name: jiamingzz/lgwm

name: Twin
notes: Twin Labs SAS, a Paris company, provides the service under its terms. Agents prefer APIs and built-in tools; the Web Agent takes over only when no API, or no API scope, covers a step, and the documentation calls it the most expensive and least reliable execution mode. It runs in an embedded browser on an isolated cloud computer dedicated to the agent. It scrapes the target page first, asks for approval of the planned browser task during the build phase, and shows a live view while it navigates, clicks and fills forms. On login pages it pauses so the user can sign in, then stores the session cookies for later runs.
summary: No-code platform that turns plain-language goals into scheduled business agents, calling APIs where they exist and falling back to a Web Agent that clicks, types and fills forms in an isolated cloud browser.

name: Starizon AI
notes: The terms of service name Starizon Ltd as the provider of the website, browser extension and related services. Agent S6 navigates, clicks, types and fills in forms in the browser session the user is already signed in to; it stops for confirmations, sign-ins, choices between options and blocked pages, and waits for the user before irreversible actions such as submitting or paying. Chat history, the Knowledge Base and Spaces are stored in the browser profile, while prompts and task context, including page screenshots when browser actions need them, go to the chosen model service or to the user's own API key. The about page claims over 70% on Online-Mind2Web with visual understanding and DOM preprocessing; that score, reliability and pricing terms are publisher statements.
summary: Chrome side-panel agent that researches across tabs, bookmarks and a local knowledge base, and hands click-and-type tasks on signed-in sites to its Agent S6 browser agent, with replays, schedules and page monitors.

name: Computer Agent Arena: Toward Human-Centric Evaluation and Analysis of Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2026 proceedings page and abstract, the full proceedings PDF and the platform README at commit 4536036; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2026 Poster. Two anonymized agents run the same user-written instruction in parallel, identically initialized Ubuntu or Windows virtual machines on AWS EC2, shown to users through a browser VNC view and synchronized replays; the paper turns the pairwise votes into a Bradley-Terry ranking and also collects optional step-level labels. It reports 2,201 filtered votes from 1,058 users over 12 agents, compares pure GUI agents with agents that also call tools or write code, and links github.com/xlang-ai/computer-agent-arena for the platform and a Hugging Face page for the collected data; neither release was reviewed here. No arXiv version was found.

name: Learning to Contextualize Web Pages for Enhanced Decision Making by LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2025 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2025 Poster. LCoW's contextualization module reads the task, previous actions and a raw page observation such as an accessibility tree, and is retrained each iteration by supervised fine-tuning on the sampled rewrites that let several LLM agents recover the ground-truth action in successful trajectories. Appendix B fine-tunes Phi-3-mini-Instruct for WebShop and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for WorkArena and WebArena. WebShop and WorkArena are the main benchmarks; a 165-task WebArena subset tests generalization to unseen task types. The same paper is posted on arXiv as 2503.10689 with the comment "Accepted to ICLR 2025". The paper points to lcowiclr2025.github.io for code.

The built-in assistant Moss creates, schedules and debugs tasks from chat and is also reachable from coding agents through an MCP server. The agent's model is unspecified.

name: Uni-GUI-OpenMobile
notes: The UI-MOPD paper's Uni-GUI combines self-collected trajectories with cleaned public OpenCUA and OpenMobile (arxiv:2604.15093) trajectories, and its composition table lists a mobile OpenMobile part of about 2.7K trajectories and 35K steps; this repository's name and 2,640 trajectories match that part, though its card describes the data only as collected on open-source apps via AndroidWorld and reports about 25.9K steps. Episode IDs carry split1 to split4 prefixes. Every folder also has a result.json (a sampled one holds the goal and raw per-step model responses with tool calls), and 1,913 folders have a metadata.json. Apache-2.0 is the card's declaration and does not settle rights to the upstream trajectories or app content.

name: Multimodal-Mind2Web
notes: Each row is one action step with the page state before the action; tasks are distinct annotation IDs. The card says the three test splits were human-verified for element visibility and rendering, while the train split may contain badly rendered screenshots. Its test task counts (177, 142 and 694) are lower than the 252, 177 and 912 task instances that the Mind2Web README lists for the cross-task, cross-website and cross-domain test sets. The card points to the SeeAct repository and paper and declares OpenRAIL, recorded as stated; terms for the underlying website content were not assessed.

name: WebsiteBench
notes: Each task folder has instruction.md, task.toml, an agent environment with a browser gateway and reference website, an oracle solution and a hidden verifier; manifest.json records file hashes. The full set is 9.7 GB, each environment requests 8 CPUs, 8 GiB memory and 20 GiB disk, and code and task definitions are Apache-2.0.
summary: Hugging Face copy of the 70 WebsiteBench tasks in Harbor format, where agents explore a production-level reference website in a browser and rebuild a full-stack clone scored by hidden functional and visual tests.

name: Gumloop
notes: Recorded as adjacent: Gumloop presents itself as a platform for building, sharing and running AI agents for business teams, which work mainly through app connectors, MCP servers and APIs, and its help pages advise using the agent browser only when no connector or API covers a task. The agent browser is an ability turned on per custom agent, and on Enterprise organizations it is off by default until an admin adds it to a role. It runs Chromium on the agent's computer, which shares the agent's code sandbox, and opens pages, clicks, types, scrolls and switches tabs. Gumloop types saved logins and 2FA codes for the agent without showing them to the model, keeps sign-ins in browser profiles, offers residential proxies and desktop or Pixel 7 mobile emulation, and pauses to hand the live browser to a person at logins, CAPTCHAs or purchase confirmations. Every browser step is recorded for replay. Agents can also be reached from Slack, Microsoft Teams, email and text messages.
summary: Business agent platform whose agents work through app connectors and can turn on a Chromium browser that clicks, types, signs in with saved logins and hands control to a person when a site needs it.

name: dart-gui-7b
notes: Seven safetensors shards with tokenizer and chat template files. The DART-GUI repository provides inference, environment, sampling and training code with Docker setups, and its training setup downloads UI-TARS-1.5-7B as the starting checkpoint.
summary: GUI agent checkpoint released with DART, a decoupled asynchronous RL framework that separates environments, rollout, data management and training; the paper reports 42.13% task success on OSWorld.

name: Narada Operator
notes: Narada says the product offers session monitoring and replay, sensitive-workflow takeover modes, and a Chrome extension for trying the consumer version.
summary: Narada Operator is an enterprise web agent that executes workflows across web interfaces and APIs using task planning and error recovery.

name: HyperWrite Personal Assistant
notes: The site footer names OthersideAI as the publisher of HyperWrite, which its llms.txt describes mainly as an AI writing and productivity assistant with a document editor, TypeAhead sentence prediction in a Chrome extension, Personas and a library of AI tools. The Personal Assistant page presents HyperWrite's AI agent as able to use the browser to complete tasks, with examples such as organizing a Gmail inbox, booking a flight, ordering a pizza and finding candidates on LinkedIn. The AI Agent tool page says the agent executes tasks in the user's browser through the HyperWrite extension, searching, navigating websites, filling out forms and interacting with web applications, and lists a limited free trial with paid Premium and Ultra plans. The Personal Assistant page also carries writing and research copy and leftover placeholder text, and its FAQ describes only the extension's writing features. The agent's model, current availability and reliability remain unverified in the reviewed evidence.
summary: Browser agent from HyperWrite that carries out typed requests such as searching, making reservations and filling out forms by operating the user's Chrome browser through the HyperWrite extension.

name: GTA1-7B-2507

name: Are CAPTCHAs Still Bot-hard? Generalized Visual CAPTCHA Solving with Agentic Vision Language Model
notes: Reviewed against the USENIX Security 2025 proceedings PDF and the authors' project page halligan.pages.dev, which the paper names as its website. In the benchmark comparison Halligan used GPT-4o and acted through PyAutoGUI on CAPTCHAs replayed from a local Flask server. The paper reports 1,577 of 2,600 benchmark challenges solved (60.7%) and a 70.6% average solve rate on previously unseen CAPTCHAs over a 30-day field study run through human-driven CAPTCHA farms. It names Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.15580923 for its source code and benchmark. No arXiv version was found.
summary: Presents Halligan, a VLM agent that abstracts visual CAPTCHAs into frames, elements and keypoints and solves each as a search problem through generated interaction code, tested on 2,600 challenges of 26 types.
