name: SATraj-OS
notes: The ungated Hub repository (revision 74deb768) publishes trajectories.jsonl files with zipped or tarred step screenshots in three configs: Capability (tasks from SCOPE-Gen), Safety-v2 (safe completions and refusals on attack-injected Capability tasks) and a legacy Safety archive generated through RiOSWorld rollouts that keeps risky outcomes. Each record has chat-format messages whose assistant turns hold an action description and a coordinate action, plus success, safety, reward and attack fields. The card declares Apache-2.0 for the data; screenshots show third-party desktop applications whose own terms are not addressed. Thunderbird and VLC capability files are present outside the capability config. The Safactory report (arXiv 2605.06230, v2) describes SATraj-OS as produced with its OSGym environment and reports 10,496 trajectories and 158,196 steps. That paper is not yet in the retained archive, so no paper relation is recorded.

The current homepage presents browser control (navigating tabs, filling forms) as one of four capabilities beside an operational graph, an editable knowledge manual and event- or schedule-triggered agents that work through integrations with Gmail, Slack, CRMs and other tools. The prompts in its use-case library mostly name connected apps such as HubSpot, Gmail, Slack and Notion; the scope is adjacent to browser actions. The pricing page lists the browser extension among the features of its paid individual plans, and the homepage marks a desktop app as coming soon. The models behind the agents, reliability and the security and privacy claims are publisher statements.

name: Ace

The About page says Ace learns from experts' screen recordings with mouse and keyboard logs, and that General Agents is developing video-language-action models. The official Python client (generalagents-python 0.1.1 at commit d36f6a8) posts a WebP screenshot, the instruction and recent actions to /v1/control/predict on api.generalagents.com; its macOS Computer class captures the screen with screencapture and performs clicks, drags, scrolls, key presses and typing through pyautogui. Apache-2.0 covers the client's code. At review time api.generalagents.com and docs.generalagents.com had DNS resolution failures; the reviewed pages leave pricing, download and sign-up paths unspecified, so current availability remains unknown.

name: OSWorld-V2 0624 Codex attempt trajectories
notes: The card calls this a self-reported trajectory package; it links no paper or harness code, and the run was not listed in the official OSWorld-V2 leaderboard data when checked on 2026-10-18. run_manifest.json records benchmark release osworld-v2-2026.06.24, a Docker provider with a QEMU backend at 1920x1080, a 400-step limit, a screenshot at every step with accessibility tree and OCR on demand, and a multi-attempt policy with one reported result per task. Per task_results.csv, 83 reported results come from initial attempts, 22 from recovery attempts and 3 from retries; the preview table names a different selected attempt for 6 tasks, and the manifest and summary.json give different recovery limits (2 and 3). Each attempt has a card written as instructions to the agent: the solution card opened for task 001 lists the exact schedule entries to enter, the events to delete and the final checks, and the recovery card opened for task 002 plans a guided retry from its parent attempt. summary.json reports a mean score of 0.661 and 43 binary passes over 108 tasks (the preview table marks 44 because task 015 scores 0.9999999999999999); these are publisher measurements from guided, multi-attempt runs. Linux is established from the Ubuntu Calendar target and /home/user shell commands in task 001. The card declares no license.
summary: Self-reported OSWorld-V2 run of a Codex-based harness with gpt-5.6-sol on all 108 tasks: per-step CLI and GUI actions, screenshots and scores, plus retried attempts and the solution and recovery cards that guided them.

name: UI-Hawk: Unleashing the Screen Stream Understanding for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the EMNLP 2025 proceedings page and the full proceedings PDF. The PDF (10.9 MB) exceeds the receipt size limit, so the retained receipt is the landing page with its complete abstract. Per the PDF, UI-Hawk replaces TextHawk's language model with Qwen2-7B and encodes each history screenshot at a quarter of its size in 144 visual tokens; FunUI holds 2,150 Chinese and 9,347 English Android screens, and navigation is evaluated on GUI-Odyssey+ (GUIOdyssey clicks re-annotated with element boxes) and the authors' Chinese GUI-Zouwu episodes. An earlier version titled 'UI-Hawk: Unleashing the Screen Stream Understanding for GUI Agents' was posted on Preprints.org on 30 August 2024 (DOI 10.20944/preprints202408.2137.v1) by the same six authors. The paper points to github.com/IMNearth/UIHawk for code and data.
summary: Mobile GUI agent whose history-aware visual encoder reads earlier screenshots with the current one, trained by a curriculum from grounding, referring, screen QA and summarization to navigation; adds the FunUI benchmark.

name: Firecrawl
notes: Recorded as adjacent: the publisher presents Firecrawl as a web data API for AI agents, and its search, scrape, map and crawl endpoints return page content as Markdown, HTML, JSON or screenshots without operating the page. Interact continues from a scrape result: POST /v2/scrape/{scrapeId}/interact takes either a natural-language prompt, which it carries out by clicking, typing and scrolling, or Playwright code, and returns a CDP URL and live-view URLs; named profiles keep browser state such as logins between sessions. The Browser Sandbox (POST /v2/interact) opens a standalone isolated browser session with Playwright and the agent-browser CLI preinstalled, CDP access and an embeddable interactive live view. The /agent endpoint gathers data from a prompt by searching and navigating sites and runs on the publisher's Spark 2 model. The homepage HTML changes on every request, so the primary receipt is the documentation introduction. The homepage also links the repository github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl; hosted feature coverage in that code is unreviewed.
summary: Hosted web data API for AI agents that searches and scrapes pages into Markdown or JSON, with an Interact endpoint and browser sandbox in which prompts or Playwright code click, type and fill forms.

name: In-Context Teacher–Student Guidance for Open-Weight Browser Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the publisher PDF and the Crossref deposit for its DOI. The method, In-Context Learning Guidance (ICLG), has GPT-5.1 solve tasks offline and appends its reasoning fields alone to the student prompt; the teacher's low-level actions stay outside that prompt, and teacher calls precede the student run. Evaluation serves the 130 MiniWoB++ tasks locally, caps each run at 5 minutes and 25 interaction steps, counts a score of at least 0.5 as solved, and reports single runs: seven of ten students improve and three lose one task. Retry and refined-prompt ablations cover three students. The paper names no code release or arXiv version.
summary: Training-free protocol that turns a teacher model's offline reasoning traces into prompt guidance for open-weight browser agents; on MiniWoB++ it lifts solved student-task pairs from 208 to 271 across ten students.

name: UiPath ScreenPlay
notes: UiPath describes Screen Agent as the agentic framework behind the ScreenPlay activity in UiPath Studio and Studio Web: a planner turns intent into high-level action sequences, and a targeter that combines a grounder with UiPath's AI Computer Vision resolves pixel coordinates before acting; ScreenPlay adds AI-based DOM extraction. The installation guide offers out-of-the-box Screen Agent variants with Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, GPT-5 and GPT-5 mini, as well as OpenAI Operator and Anthropic computer use, or bring-your-own-model connections to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex or an OpenAI V1-compatible provider. UiPath's January 2026 press release and blog report a 67.1% OSWorld-Verified score for the Claude Opus 4.5 variant, then ranked first, and the blog says UiPath also evaluates Screen Agent on its UI-CUBE benchmark; these are publisher statements.

The updates log dates a DLAM early-access preview for desktop control via r1 on Windows and Mac to 29 January 2026, BYOK support for DLAM with Anthropic and OpenAI keys to rabbitOS 2.3 (10 July 2026), and OS3 general availability to 22 September 2026. Earlier r1 releases shipped LAM playground, a web agent acting through a webdriver from visual and structured input (1 October 2024), and teach mode, which learned website tasks from demonstrations (21 November 2024); the current user guide describes neither.

notes: Built as the per-step decision head of the jev-ultrafast browser agent. The remote code builds each request from the page URL, title, up to 1,200 characters of page text, the interactive elements with their roles and the last ten actions; it takes no screenshot, and a separate local LLM writes the text that TYPE_TEXT enters. The repository also ships a jev-ultrafast-compatible server, evaluation suites, training pipeline code, a harness patch and result logs. The card reports 11 to 14 of 54 multi-step tasks on held-out real sites for version v19s and 22 to 27 ms per decision on one RTX 4070 Ti SUPER; these are publisher measurements. The card metadata declares Apache-2.0 and says the training datasets keep their own licenses.

name: CloudCruise
notes: The homepage targets payer-portal and EHR workflows and says every run executes in a VM with laptop-like fingerprints and human-like input, with queued concurrency, video replay, per-action screenshots and logs, and HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. The documentation says the builder agent opens a live browser preview, navigates the target site, asks clarifying questions and turns confirmed actions into a node-and-edge graph that later runs deterministically, with model calls confined to building the graph. Click nodes target elements either by XPath or through an LLM vision mode labelled AI (Screenshot). The maintenance agent classifies failures from the error screenshot, page state and selector signals, then recovers in place, asks for input, retries or hands the workflow to the builder agent. Citrix virtual desktops are automated through their HTML5 browser client using the screenshot mode. Runs start through an API with TypeScript and Python SDKs.
summary: Managed browser-automation platform for healthcare portals and EHRs in which a builder agent turns a chat description into a reusable workflow graph that runs in cloud VMs and a maintenance agent repairs.

name: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Model in GUI World
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2025 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2025 Poster. The grounding model, AssistGUIGrounder (AGG), pairs a SAM-pretrained ViT image encoder and a transformer query encoder with a two-layer box decoder. The data engine loads Common Crawl pages from 118 domains in a browser such as Chrome, scrolls them with Page Down and reads element data through UI Automation; grounding training used 0.36M web images with 22M annotations after smoothing, plus 27K mobile screenshots from WidgetCaption and RICO. ScreenSpot grounding covers mobile, desktop and web screenshots; agent fine-tuning covers MiniWob, AITW and Mind2Web. The paper gives github.com/showlab/AssistGUIGround for code and data; that repository returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-19. No arXiv version was found.

name: AdapAction: Adaptive Target Action Backdoor Attack against GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the CVF open-access landing page and PDF. A teacher model (for example Gemini 2.5 Pro) writes malicious reasoning trajectories drawn from a five-category malicious action library, and the agent learns them by supervised fine-tuning, which the paper calls Context-Aware Behavioral Imitation. Main results fine-tune Qwen2-VL-2B and Qwen2-VL-7B at a 0.1 poisoning ratio with a blended visual trigger; an AndroidWorld emulator deployment through Mobile-Agent-v3 is described in the supplementary material. The paper links no code release or arXiv version.
summary: Backdoor attack that fine-tunes GUI agents on teacher-written malicious trajectories, so a trigger makes the agent choose a harmful action fitting the current screen and instruction; tested on AitZ and AndroidControl.

name: Yutori
notes: Yutori was founded by Abhishek Das, Devi Parikh and Dhruv Batra and announced its seed round in March 2025. Navigator models are called through an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint: the caller sends a screenshot and a task, the model returns actions as tool calls, and the caller executes them and sends a fresh screenshot in an agent loop. n1.5 drives browsers in a normalized 1000x1000 coordinate space with a core set of 18 coordinate-based tools or an expanded set that adds element extraction, find, set_element_value and JavaScript execution, and can return JSON matching a caller schema. n2 operates a full desktop through batched GUI actions plus bash and file tools; the SDK ships local Docker and Daytona examples, and Yutori MCP runs it on the visible macOS desktop, sending screen contents to Yutori. A Python SDK wraps the APIs, a CLI runs research, browsing and Scout tasks, and an MCP server with workflow skills exposes these tasks and computer use to coding agents. Scouts monitor the web on a schedule, and Delegate is a consumer agent meant to complete handed-off tasks independently. Yutori also publishes a computer-use leaderboards page compiling reported results for six benchmarks. The publisher describes its Online-Mind2Web figure as independently verified and its Navi-Bench v2 and Westworld figures as its own evaluations.
summary: Yutori's web-agent platform: the Navigator computer-use model API (n1.5 for browsers, n2 for full desktops), task APIs for browsing, research and Scout web monitoring, and the Delegate personal agent.
